SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these should a good county sketch map have? (1 mark)
   A. A photograph of the teacher
   B. A picture of a tractor
   C. A recipe
   D. A title

2. A pupil says that a county with many people must be the biggest in area. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Counties never have people
   B. People make land bigger
   C. Only farms make counties big
   D. Area and population are different things

3. How many counties does Kenya have? (1 mark)
   A. 37
   B. 27
   C. 57
   D. 47

4. Which is the largest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Mombasa
   B. Turkana
   C. Nairobi
   D. Kisumu

5. What is a river? (1 mark)
   A. Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   B. A steep hill
   C. A flat plain
   D. A big lake

6. Which of these is not a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A monument
   B. A cultural centre
   C. A natural river
   D. A museum

7. Why is population distribution useful to county planners? (1 mark)
   A. It helps them to move rivers
   B. It helps them to change the weather
   C. It helps them to grow tea
   D. It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live

8. Which of these is an aspect of traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. Traditional food
   B. Rainfall
   C. Mountains
   D. Rivers

9. Which is a ceremony? (1 mark)
   A. A rainy day
   B. A wedding
   C. A road
   D. A market

10. What should you do if you break a school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Blame others
   B. Run away
   C. Hide it
   D. Say sorry and accept fair guidance

11. Which of these is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. Singing at bedtime
   B. Watching clouds
   C. Fishing
   D. Sleeping

12. Where are fish processing factories found? (1 mark)
   A. On the shores of Lake Victoria
   B. In a desert without water
   C. In the sky
   D. On top of Mount Kenya

13. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. The price of a book
   B. All the money spent
   C. Money borrowed
   D. Money left after paying all costs

14. What does the project manager do? (1 mark)
   A. Prints books
   B. Cooks lunch
   C. Drives the bus
   D. Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time

15. Wanjiru sold 10 tomatoes but recorded only 8. What should she do? (1 mark)
   A. Hide the money
   B. Blame a friend
   C. Keep quiet
   D. Correct the record and tell the treasurer

16. Which of these is an honest practice in business? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating customers
   B. Selling bad goods as good
   C. Hiding sales money
   D. Giving correct change

17. Being good even when nobody is watching is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Punishment
   B. Integrity
   C. Boasting
   D. Fashion

18. Which action shows responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. Doing your class duty without being reminded
   B. Breaking things
   C. Refusing to help
   D. Waiting to be told each time

19. What should you do if you are very angry? (1 mark)
   A. Break something
   B. Shout insults
   C. Walk away and calm down
   D. Hit someone

20. What is forgiveness? (1 mark)
   A. Punishing without listening
   B. Ignoring the wrong
   C. Keeping anger forever
   D. Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you

21. In an election, 12 pupils voted for Amina and 10 for Brian. Who wins? (1 mark)
   A. Amina
   B. Nobody
   C. Brian
   D. Both

22. Why should voting be secret? (1 mark)
   A. So that nobody can force how you vote
   B. So that the winner is hidden
   C. So that votes are lost
   D. So that nobody counts

23. What is an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   B. A kind of food
   C. A game
   D. A sports match

24. Which is a function of the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   B. Setting exams
   C. Beating pupils
   D. Collecting fees

25. What is a Children's Government in school? (1 mark)
   A. A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
   B. A group of teachers
   C. The government of Kenya
   D. A group of parents

26. Which is the right way to make a complaint? (1 mark)
   A. By fighting
   B. Through your class representative
   C. By spreading rumours
   D. By shouting in class

27. Who leads a sub-location? (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. President
   C. Governor
   D. Assistant chief

28. Which of these is a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. A trader
   B. A farmer
   C. A pastor
   D. A driver

29. Which action shows good leadership? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   B. Hiding the food
   C. Keeping all the food
   D. Giving only to friends

30. Which of these is a county government service? (1 mark)
   A. Issuing passports
   B. Running the army
   C. Running county health centres
   D. Defending the country

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. How do you calculate profit? (2 marks)

32. Name the four cardinal points. (2 marks)

33. Explain what jua kali workers do and why they are important. (4 marks)

34. Give three ethical practices in managing a school enterprise. (3 marks)

35. Give two responsibilities of a child at school. (2 marks)

36. Explain the difference between clustered and scattered settlement. (3 marks)

37. Give four school rules and one reason for each. (4 marks)

38. Explain why it is important to keep records of income and costs. (3 marks)

39. Give two reasons why some areas are densely populated. (2 marks)

40. State three benefits of democracy in school. (3 marks)

41. Describe how to draw a dot map showing population distribution in your county. (4 marks)

42. Plan a class culture day. State five things you would include. (5 marks)

43. Give three examples of artefacts and say how each is used. (3 marks)

44. Name two landforms and two water features. (4 marks)

45. Explain three rules of good digital citizenship. (3 marks)

46. Describe how a pupil can help a new pupil to settle in. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — A title
   A good map has a title, a north arrow and a key.

2. D — Area and population are different things
   Size is about area. Population is the number of people.

3. D — 47
   The Constitution of Kenya 2010 created 47 counties.

4. B — Turkana
   Turkana is the largest county by land area.

5. A — Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   Rivers flow along channels towards a lake or an ocean.

6. C — A natural river
   A river is a natural feature, not built by people.

7. D — It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   Services should reach people where they live.

8. A — Traditional food
   Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, games and ceremonies are aspects of culture.

9. B — A wedding
   A wedding is a special event with customs.

10. D — Say sorry and accept fair guidance
   We should be honest and accept correction.

11. C — Fishing
   Fishing produces food and income.

12. A — On the shores of Lake Victoria
   Fish are processed near the lake where they are caught.

13. D — Money left after paying all costs
   Profit = income - costs.

14. D — Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   The manager coordinates the work.

15. D — Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   Records must be honest and complete.

16. D — Giving correct change
   Honesty is right in business.

17. B — Integrity
   Integrity means doing right when unseen.

18. A — Doing your class duty without being reminded
   Responsible pupils do their duties.

19. C — Walk away and calm down
   Cooling down prevents harm.

20. D — Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you
   Forgiveness ends quarrels.

21. A — Amina
   12 is more than 10.

22. A — So that nobody can force how you vote
   Secret voting protects free choice.

23. A — A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   An agenda gives the order of business.

24. A — Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   Leaders help with order and cleanliness.

25. A — A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
   It is made up of pupils chosen by their classmates.

26. B — Through your class representative
   Use proper channels.

27. D — Assistant chief
   An assistant chief leads a sub-location.

28. C — A pastor
   Pastors lead worship.

29. A — Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   Fairness and honesty are good leadership.

30. C — Running county health centres
   Health centres are a county responsibility.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Profit is found by subtracting the costs from the income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for costs from income.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: North, east, south and west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct points, 2 marks for all four.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: They make and repair goods such as furniture and metal doors in small workshops. They give jobs, provide cheap goods, and train young people in skills.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Be honest with money and customers, be fair in sharing work and rewards, and care for the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each practice.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attend and study hard, and respect others. Accept care for property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each responsibility.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clustered means homes are close together in a group, for example around a town. Scattered means homes are far apart from each other.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for a clear contrast.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Come on time to avoid missing lessons; keep the school clean for health; respect others for peace; care for property so it lasts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule with a reason.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: To know whether there is profit or loss, to show honesty, and to plan better next time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Good rain and fertile soil for farming, and jobs and services in towns. Accept water or good roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone has a voice, decisions are fair, and pupils obey rules they helped to make.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county boundary. Decide how many people one dot stands for. Put more dots where more people live and fewer dots where few live. Add a title and key.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Traditional dress, foods to taste, songs and dances, artefacts on display, and stories told by elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clay pot for cooking or storing water, a basket for carrying items, and a stool for sitting. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct artefact with use.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Landforms: mountain and valley (or hill, plain, plateau). Water features: lake and river (or waterfall, ocean).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult before going online, do not share private information, and be kind and never bully online.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome the pupil, show the classrooms and toilets, and invite the pupil to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.
